also_called: Large Language Model (LLM) and Transformer Architecture
one_liner: A chatbot is an advanced autocomplete: it predicts the next small piece of text, adds it, and repeats.

steps.title: Text is broken into tokens
steps.text: When you type a prompt, the system slices your words into small fragments called tokens (roughly four letters each).

stage_state.description: Incoming sentence split into numbered token blocks.

steps.title: Scores every candidate word
steps.text: The model calculates probabilities for thousands of possible next tokens based on patterns learned during training.

stage_state.description: Bar charts rise showing percentage likelihood for top candidate tokens.

steps.title: Picks one token and repeats
steps.text: It selects one candidate token, attaches it to the text, and feeds the entire updated paragraph back into the engine to predict the next word.

stage_state.description: Chosen token attaches to the sentence, cycling to the next position.

steps.title: Pattern fluency is distinct from verified truth
steps.text: Because the engine optimizes for plausible-sounding phrasing, an answer can read like deliberate thinking even when the underlying claim is incorrect.

stage_state.description: Visual indicator showing plausible linguistic coherence alongside factual verification check.

analogy.text: Think of it like smart phone autocomplete that has studied millions of books. A reader with a highlighter (the attention mechanism) skims backwards across earlier words to decide which ideas connect.
analogy.breaks: A human understands the physical meaning behind sentences. The model calculates statistical relationships between text tokens, and multiple attention heads run in parallel across dozens of layers.

myth.claim: A chatbot looks up live information on the web by default.
myth.reality: Standard models answer purely from patterns stored in their internal parameters unless connected to a search tool or private files.

seen_in: Email smart compose and sentence completion

persona_examples.student: Why an AI helper can invent an academic citation that looks authentic but leads to a non-existent paper.
persona_examples.teacher: Why student drafts generated with AI sound articulate and fluent yet sometimes assert incorrect historical dates.
persona_examples.entrepreneur: Why language models vary in phrasing across runs, making prompt constraints and automated testing essential.
persona_examples.engineer_office: How context window boundaries determine how many pages of meeting notes can be pasted at once.

quiz.question: What fundamental action does a language model perform at each step?
options: It searches an indexed database of verified facts
It predicts the most probable next token and repeats
It verifies whether the user is authorized to ask the question
It executes Python code to solve the prompt
quiz.explanation: A language model operates as a statistical next-token predictor, generating text one piece at a time.

quiz.question: Why can an AI response sound completely confident while stating an untrue fact?
options: The model is intentionally trying to mislead users
It was trained to optimize for persuasive grammar and plausible patterns, not verified truth
The computer ran out of memory while typing
quiz.explanation: Language models predict fluent text based on statistical likelihood rather than checking facts against reality.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of the attention mechanism (the transformer core)?
options: To make the font size larger for headings
To allow words in a sentence to connect with other relevant words regardless of distance
To reduce power consumption of computer cooling fans
To translate speech into video files
quiz.explanation: Attention allows every word to look at all other words simultaneously, linking pronouns and context across long paragraphs.

explain_back.prompt: Complete this sentence to prove you understand:
explain_back.template: A chatbot works by predicting the next probable token repeatedly, which is why it can sound articulate even when stating an unverified fact.

bullets: Text is encoded into discrete tokens (using BPE or WordPiece algorithms) and mapped to high-dimensional embedding vectors.
Stacked transformer layers apply Multi-Head Self-Attention (Query, Key, Value dot-products) followed by Feed-Forward Networks.
The final linear projection and Softmax layer produce a probability distribution over the full vocabulary (~128k tokens).
Decoding strategies (temperature, top-p, top-k) balance predictable greediness against creative divergence.

code_panel.title: Minimal Next-Token Generation Loop
code_panel.code:
# Minimal autoregressive generation loop (pseudocode)
tokens = tokenizer.encode(prompt)
for _ in range(max_new_tokens):
    logits = model(tokens)                  # [batch, seq_len, vocab_size]
    next_token_logits = logits[:, -1, :] / temperature
    probs = softmax(next_token_logits, dim=-1)
    next_token = sample(probs, top_p=0.9)  # Pick next token
    tokens.append(next_token)
    if next_token == tokenizer.eos_token_id:
        break
return tokenizer.decode(tokens)
